terms.comment: Ancient terminology need not map exactly onto a single modern species. The alternate stem cucum- also occurs in ancient inflection; cucumer is a later or variant dictionary form, not required for ordinary use here. English cucumber ultimately comes from Latin through French; the deeper origin of the Latin word is uncertain.

sources: The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 69; p. 71; p. 299.
